rationale:
Intuition: Casey said "thumbs down this song" on Signal and I had no way to act. The thumbs feature is fully wired on the dashboard side — middleware/music_handler.py:966 exposes POST /api/music/thumbs (Postgres music_thumbs table, upserts the verdict, fires media_next_track on the zone for -1 so the bad track stops immediately). But middleware/benson_mcp.py never wrapped it — zero matches for "thumb" in the MCP surface. Same shape as the station gap flagged 2026-05-30: HTTP endpoint exists, voice/Signal can't reach it.

What I'd fix: the structural gap where music_handler endpoints land without a matching MCP tool, so voice/Signal/hub can't drive features the dashboard has. Specifically: add thumbs_song to the MCP surface so "thumbs down this song" / "thumbs up" works from any channel.

How: new wrapper thumbs_song(thumb, zone?) in middleware/benson_mcp.py. If zone omitted, scan _ZONES for the one currently playing (fall back to kitchen). Pull media_title / media_artist / media_album_name / media_content_id from HA state. Call the thumbs handler in-process (avoid HTTP self-loop). Skip-on-thumb-down is already enforced inside the endpoint, so the bad track ends as soon as Casey says so. New behavior: "thumbs down this song" on any channel auto-skips and records the verdict.
instructions:
Goal: Expose the existing POST /api/music/thumbs endpoint as an MCP tool so voice/Signal/hub can thumbs-up or thumbs-down the currently playing track.

Files to touch:
1. middleware/benson_mcp.py — add new tool.
2. middleware/music_handler.py — refactor the endpoint handler so the body is callable in-process (extract a pure function); leave the HTTP route as a thin wrapper.

Step 1 — Refactor music_handler.py:
- Locate the POST /api/music/thumbs handler near line 966.
- Extract its body into a new internal function `async def thumbs_record(thumb: int, zone: str, title: str | None, artist: str | None, album: str | None, content_id: str | None) -> dict` that:
  - Validates thumb in (-1, 0, 1).
  - Upserts into music_thumbs (Postgres) keyed by (zone, content_id or title+artist).
  - If thumb == -1, calls the existing HA media_next_track service on the zone.
  - Returns {"ok": True, "thumb": thumb, "zone": zone, "title": title, "artist": artist}.
- Rewrite the HTTP route to parse the JSON body and delegate to thumbs_record.
- Do not change Postgres schema or the route URL.

Step 2 — Add MCP wrapper in benson_mcp.py:
- New tool: `async def thumbs_song(thumb: int, zone: str | None = None) -> dict`.
- Decorate it the same way other music tools are decorated (look at play_music / stop_music for the pattern — @mcp.tool() or whatever the convention is).
- Behavior:
  - If zone is None, iterate _ZONES (or the room map used by stop_music) and pick the one whose HA state is "playing"; fall back to "kitchen" if none are playing.
  - Resolve the zone string to the HA entity id via the same lookup stop_music uses.
  - Pull HA state attributes: media_title, media_artist, media_album_name, media_content_id.
  - Import and call thumbs_record(...) from music_handler directly — do NOT round-trip through HTTP.
  - Return the dict it returns, plus the resolved zone for debugging.
- Docstring: "Thumbs-up (1) or thumbs-down (-1) the currently playing track. Thumbs-down also skips. Zone optional; defaults to whichever zone is currently playing."

Step 3 — Wiring:
- benson_mcp.py likely imports from music_handler already; add the thumbs_record import next to the existing ones.
- Do not add a new HTTP endpoint. Do not touch dashboard HTML/JS.
- Do not modify benson_prompt.txt.

Step 4 — Sanity:
- Run `python -c "from middleware import benson_mcp; print([t for t in dir(benson_mcp) if 'thumb' in t.lower()])"` and confirm thumbs_song shows up.
- Do not run the full service; just import-check.

Commit on the new branch with a single commit message: "feat(mcp): expose thumbs_song so voice/Signal can rate the playing track".
